editorial:
Imagine being trapped in a place you always thought was safe, only to have ten armed militants take over and hold over a hundred people hostage. That is exactly how things kick off here. You get pulled into a high-stakes game where the bad guys aren't just looking for money, but have three very specific and stubborn demands that the government refuses to meet. The vibe is super tense from the first minute, and you will find yourself rooting for the captives while trying to figure out if the militants have a point or if they are just dangerous. It feels like a pressure cooker that is about to blow, and you will be on the edge of your seat wondering who will make it out alive.

The acting is top-notch and makes the danger feel real, and the plot twists actually surprise you instead of being obvious. While the middle part slows down a bit too much with some long talking scenes, the final act makes up for it with some wild action. If you love stories about hostage situations and political drama, you need to see this.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you find out that the militants were actually working with a double agent inside the government. The big twist is that the hostage crisis was a distraction to steal secret files. Most of the captives are saved, but the leader of the militants dies in a shootout. The movie ends with the revelation that the stolen files are already leaked online, meaning the government loses no matter what happened in the building.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves high-stakes hostage dramas and plot twists.
